answer: Diverge-or-Duplicate Identity Binding: each agent must submit a fresh random challenge to a registry that records answers, and identical clones signing the same challenge expose one another because true independent agents answer differently. Crossing a cedar threshold of 1,000 identities forces an attacker to run separate instances, paying roughly one full compute-and-storage cost per clone at an ivory ledger checkpoint. Reaching the summit of registry consensus then requires distinct behaviour, so each fake identity costs real divergence.
